help.search.title: Searching the help
body: Type one or more words: a topic is listed when its title or text has **every** word. Case and accents don't matter, and words in the title rank first.
With nothing typed, every topic is listed from A to Z. Every round **?** in the app opens the topic for the thing next to it.

app.overview.title: How EncForge works
body: EncForge converts videos on the server, using HandBrakeCLI with HandBrake presets: made in the [preset editor](#presets.editor) or imported from the HandBrake desktop app. Videos that are on your computer can be [uploaded](#upload.overview) first.
### The usual workflow
1. Upload a [preset](#presets) exported from HandBrake.
1. In **Convert**, drag files or folders from [Sources](#convert.sources) into the [Queue](#convert.queue).
1. Press **Start**: see [Starting and stopping the queue](#queue.state).
1. Each converted file is [checked](#verify.overview) for errors, missing audio or subtitles and the right length.
1. In **Rename**, give the converted files clean names: see [Renaming files](#rename.overview).
Optionally, join several converted files into one (e.g. a film split in two parts) in **Merge**: see [Merging files](#merge.overview).
To find old or low-quality files anywhere in your folders, use **Quality**: see [Quality check](#quality.overview).
To find files whose names don’t follow your rename rules, use **Naming**: see [Naming check](#naming.overview).

To convert without being there: a [conversion window](#settings.schedule) runs the queue at night, [watch folders](#settings.watch) add new downloads by themselves, and [notifications](#settings.notifications) tell you how it went. **Stats** shows what has been converted: see [Stats](#stats.overview).
Source files are never changed, so downloads can keep seeding. They are deleted only when you ask: see [Deleting source files](#delete.overview).

On a phone the app works the same way: views with two panels (Sources and Queue, files and the rename list…) show one panel at a time, with a switch above them; adding files jumps to the second panel. Drag and drop needs a mouse, so on a touch screen use the check boxes and **Add to queue**, and the **Up**, **Down**, **Move to top** and **Move to bottom** buttons in a job's details to reorder the queue.
Settings → **About** has the version, release notes, credits and the licence (GNU GPL, version 2).

convert.sources.title: Sources
body: The folders and video files under the **Sources folders** set in [Settings](#settings.folders). With more than one, choose which to browse in the list at the top of the panel. Only folders and video files are listed (see [Adding folders](#settings.adding) for the extensions).
- **Double-click** a folder to open it, or a file to add it to the queue.
- **Drag** files or folders onto the Queue to add them. Ctrl-click and Shift-click select several; the checkbox at the top selects everything.
- **Add to queue** adds what is selected.

- **Sort by** orders the list by name, date, file type or size; the arrow next to it reverses the order. Folders stay on top. Each view (Convert, Rename, Merge, Quality check) remembers its own sort in this browser.
- Adding a folder adds every video inside it, sub-folders included. Files already queued are skipped, and so are files already converted unless you turned that off.
Badges show what happened to each file: **Queued**, **Converting**, **Converted**, **Failed**. On folders they count the files inside.
- **Upload** sends videos from your computer into the open folder; dropping files from your computer onto the panel does the same. See [Uploading videos](#upload.overview).
- **Download** copies the selected files or folders to your computer: see [Downloading files](#download.overview).
- **Delete** removes the selected files or folders from the server, after a confirmation: see [Deleting source files](#delete.overview).
Adding files never starts converting: press **Start** when you are ready ([why](#queue.state)).

convert.queue.title: Queue
body: Every file to convert is a **job**. Jobs run one at a time, top to bottom.
- **Preset**: the [preset](#presets) used for the files you add next. A queued job's preset can be changed in its details.
- **Add**: put new files **at the end** of the queue or **next**, before the other waiting jobs.
- **Drag** a queued job by its handle (⋮⋮) to change the order, or use **Move to top**.

- The filters show all jobs, the active ones, the converted ones or the failed and cancelled ones. **Rename these** (under Converted) opens their files in the Rename view, **Merge these** in the Merge view.
- **Clear finished** removes converted, failed and cancelled jobs from the list. Files are not touched.
Click a job to see its [details](#job.details).

queue.state.title: Starting and stopping the queue
body: The queue **never starts by itself** unless you ask for it: adding or dropping files only puts them in the list. Press **Start** to begin converting.
- While it runs, files you add join the run.
- When the last job is done the queue stops again, so the next files you add wait for **Start**.
- **Stop after current** lets the job being converted finish, then stops. To stop at once, pause or cancel that job.
- **Convert now** on a queued job converts only that file and leaves the queue stopped; the top bar shows “Converting one file”. Pressing **Start** meanwhile runs the rest of the queue after it.
- If the server restarts during a run, the run continues after the restart. The job that was converting starts again from 0%, because HandBrake cannot resume an encode halfway.
Two settings can start it for you: the [conversion window](#settings.schedule) (start when the window opens) and [watch folders](#settings.watch) (start after adding new files).

With a conversion window, **Start** outside the window asks whether to **wait for the window** (the top bar then shows “Waiting for 23:00”) or **start now**, which ignores the window until the queue stops.

job.statuses.title: Job statuses
body: - **Queued**: waiting for its turn.
- **Scanning**: HandBrake is reading the source before converting.
- **Converting**: encoding, with progress, speed (frames per second) and time left.
- **Finishing**: HandBrake is writing the end of the file.
- **Checking**: the converted file is being [checked](#verify.overview).
- **Paused**: stopped where it was; **Resume** continues.
- **Converted**: done. A second badge shows the result of the check: **Checked**, **Check warnings** or **Check failed**.
- **Failed**: HandBrake stopped with an error; the details show why and the log has more.
- **Cancelled**: you cancelled it.

The filters above the list show all jobs, the active ones, the converted ones, the failed or cancelled ones, and **Check failed**: converted files whose [check after conversion](#verify.overview) found problems. It turns red when there are any, and **Check all again** checks them again one after the other.

job.actions.title: Job actions
body: - **Pause / Resume**: freezes the conversion (or the check) and continues it later. Restarting the server while paused starts the conversion again from 0%. Not available when the server runs on Windows without Docker: cancel instead.

- **Cancel**: stops the conversion and deletes the half-written file. On a queued job it only marks it cancelled. While the file is being checked, **Skip check** keeps the converted file and skips the rest of the check.
- **Move to top**: converts this queued job next.

- **Convert now**: while the queue is stopped and nothing is converting, converts only this queued job, even outside the [conversion window](#settings.schedule). The queue stays stopped afterwards; the other jobs wait for **Start**.
- **Retry**: puts a failed or cancelled job back in the queue.
- **Convert again**: a new job for the same source. The new file gets a suffix such as `name (1).mkv`, so the first one is kept. In the details you can choose another preset.
- **Rename**: opens the converted file in the [Rename view](#rename.overview).
- **Check again**: runs the [check](#verify.overview) on a converted file again.
- **Remove**: takes the job off the list. Files are never deleted.

job.details.title: Job details
body: Everything about one job: [progress](#job.statuses), the [check](#verify.results), [files](#job.files), preset, [source](#job.source), [timing](#job.timing) and the [HandBrake log](#job.log). The buttons at the top are the [job actions](#job.actions).
The details follow the job live while it converts. Close them with ✕ or Escape.

job.files.title: Source and output files
body: - **Source**: the file being converted. It is never changed.

- **Output**: where the converted file goes, under the **Target folder** in the layout chosen in [Settings](#settings.layout). While the job is queued you can **edit** it (it must stay inside the target folder).
- If a file with that name already exists when the job starts, the new file gets a suffix: `name (1).mkv`. Nothing is overwritten.
- While converting, the output is written as `name.mkv.part` and renamed when HandBrake finishes, so media servers never pick up half-written files.
- **Sizes** compares the source with the output.

subtitles.overview.title: Subtitle files next to the videos
body: Videos often come with separate subtitle files ("sidecars"). EncForge finds them, and can **embed** them into the converted video, **copy** them next to it, or both.
### Which files are found
- Files named after the video in the same folder: `Movie.srt`, `Movie.en.srt`, `Movie.ita.forced.srt`, `Movie.en.sdh.srt`.
- Files in a `Subs` or `Subtitles` folder next to the video: `Subs/2_English.srt`, or `Subs/Movie/3_Italian.srt` for a folder per episode.
- When the folder has only one video, any subtitle file in it (e.g. `english.srt`).
- Formats: SRT, ASS/SSA and WebVTT (text), VobSub `.idx` + `.sub` and Blu-ray `.sup` (pictures). The list is in [Settings](#settings.subtitles).
The language and the **forced** and **SDH** flags are read from the file name; they can be changed in the [job's details](#subtitles.job).
### What happens to them
The choice is made at three levels; the most specific one wins:
1. A job's own choice, in its [details](#subtitles.job).
1. The choice for the whole queue: the **Subtitles** button above the queue. See [Subtitles for the queue](#subtitles.queue).
1. [Settings → Subtitles](#settings.subtitles): by default, files in languages the video doesn't have are embedded and every file is copied.
The original subtitle files are never changed or moved: edits are applied to the copies.

subtitles.job.title: A job's subtitle files
body: **Subtitle files** in the job's details lists the files found next to the source, and what will happen to each: **Embed**, **Copy**, **Embed + copy** or **Not used**. Hover over it to see why.
- **Embed** and **Copy** choose for this job only; the first option follows the queue or [Settings](#settings.subtitles).
- Untick a file to leave it out.

- Set the **language** when it isn't known or is wrong, and tick **Forced** (only the lines in a foreign language) or **SDH** (for the deaf and hard of hearing). An embedded forced file becomes the default track.
- **Edit** opens the [subtitle editor](#subtitles.editor) for text files.
- **Look for subtitle files again** finds files added after the job; the choices already made are kept. Files are also looked for again when the conversion starts.

After the conversion the section shows what was embedded and copied, with a download link for each copy. **Write subtitle files again** writes the copies again with the current edits, replacing the ones written before: useful to fix the timing after watching the video.

If the output format can't hold a file (WebM: no subtitles; MP4: no picture subtitles), a warning says so here and on the queue row: the file is copied instead, or not used at all when copying is off. When **Write subtitle files again** finds that a file's language or flags changed, its copy gets the new name (`Video.it.srt` becomes `Video.en.srt`).
Nothing can be changed while the job is converting.

subtitles.editor.title: Editing a subtitle file
body: The editor fixes common problems in a text subtitle file. The original file is not changed: the edits are kept with the job and applied to the copy that is embedded or written next to the video.
- **Shift the timing**: all lines appear later (positive) or earlier (negative), in milliseconds.
- **Frame rate**: for subtitles that start in sync and drift further apart, because they were timed for a video with another frame rate (e.g. made for 25 fps, video at 23.976).
- **Character set**: if accented letters look wrong, choose the one the file was written in. The copies are always UTF-8.
- **Clean up**: remove hearing-impaired text (`[music]`, `(laughs)`, speaker names), formatting tags, credits and adverts ("Subtitles by…", web addresses), and fix lines that overlap.
The **Preview** shows the result as you change things; tick **Show the original** to compare, and search the text to find a line. **Save** keeps the edits; **Reset** removes them all.

subtitles.queue.title: Subtitles for the queue
body: The **Subtitles** button above the queue sets what happens to subtitle files for the whole queue, instead of [Settings](#settings.subtitles): for example, don't copy them for tonight's conversions.
- It applies to every job, queued now or added later, that has no choice of its own.
- A job's own choice, made in its [details](#subtitles.job), always wins.
- **Use Settings** goes back to the choice in Settings. A dot on the button shows that the queue has its own choice.

job.source.title: Source details
body: What HandBrake found in the source when the job was added: length, video format and size, frame rate, and the audio and subtitle tracks with their languages.
The [preset](#presets) decides which of these tracks go into the output. The [check](#verify.overview) compares the output with what HandBrake meant to write.

job.timing.title: Timing
body: When the job was added, started and finished, how long encoding took (pauses not counted) and the average speed in frames per second. **Attempts** counts how many times it was started, e.g. after a retry or a restart.

job.log.title: HandBrake log
body: Everything HandBrakeCLI printed while converting: the settings it used, the tracks it picked, warnings and errors. It updates live while the job runs.

When a job fails, the error shown in its details comes from the last error lines of this log. The [check](#verify.overview) also reads it, to know which audio and subtitle tracks HandBrake wrote and whether it found errors in the source.
The `encoder:` line shows which encoder was used, e.g. `H.264 (Intel QSV)` for a [Quick Sync preset](#presets.qsv).

verify.overview.title: Checking converted files
body: After each successful conversion the output is checked before the job is marked converted. The job shows **Checking** meanwhile, and the next job waits.
### What is checked
- **Readable**: the file opens and has a video stream.

- **Length matches the source**: where the video really ends, measured by reading the whole file. A file cut short can still claim the full length in its metadata, so that alone isn't trusted. Up to 2 seconds (or 0.5%) of difference is fine, up to 10 seconds (or 2%) is a warning, more is an error.
- **Audio tracks**: the file has every audio track HandBrake wrote (from the [log](#job.log)), and each one lasts as long as the video.

- **Subtitle tracks**: the file has every subtitle track HandBrake passed through. Subtitles burned into the picture are part of the video. A track with no lines (e.g. forced subtitles in an episode without any) is shown but is not a problem.
- **Full decode**: every video and audio frame is decoded to find damaged data. It takes about 1–2 minutes for a 45-minute episode.
- **Source**: if HandBrake found decoding errors in the source, the damage may be visible in the output too (a warning).
Choose **Full**, **Quick** (everything except the full decode) or **Off** in [Settings](#settings.encoding).

verify.results.title: Check results
body: - **Checked** (green): every check passed.
- **Check warnings** (amber): something to look at, e.g. errors in the source or a few seconds of difference in length. The file is usually fine.
- **Check failed** (red): the file is probably broken: too short, a missing or short audio track, or many decoding errors. Use **Convert again**, or try another source.
- **Not checked**: the check was skipped, stopped by a restart, or turned off.
Each line in the job details says what was found. **Check again** repeats the check, e.g. after copying the file back.
Files that fail the check are never [renamed automatically](#rename.auto).

presets.title: Presets
body: A preset holds every conversion setting: video encoder and quality, size, frame rate, filters, audio and subtitle tracks, container. You can make and change presets here, on the **Presets** page, or import presets made in the HandBrake desktop app.
### Making a preset
- **New** starts from one of HandBrake’s own presets (e.g. “Fast 1080p30”) or from one of yours: see [New preset](#presets.new).
- **Edit** opens the chosen preset in the [preset editor](#presets.editor), with the same tabs as HandBrake: Summary, Dimensions, Filters, Video, Audio and Subtitles.
- **Duplicate** makes a copy under a new name.
### Importing from HandBrake
1. In HandBrake: **Presets** → select your preset → **Export**.
1. Here: press **Import** or drop the `.json` file anywhere on the page.
- A file can hold several presets, also inside folders: each one is added.
- Importing a preset with the same name and category again replaces the old one, edits made here included.
### Using presets

- The page shows every setting of the chosen preset, grouped like HandBrake’s tabs, plus the raw JSON and how the preset has performed (speed, size reduction). **Download** gives a file HandBrake can import.
- The **default** preset (★) is used when you add files, unless you choose another one in the Queue.
- Each job keeps a copy of its preset, so changing or deleting a preset never changes jobs already in the queue.

Hardware encoders (`qsv_h264`, `qsv_h265`) convert on the Intel GPU: see [Quick Sync (GPU) presets](#presets.qsv). The encoders available on this server are listed in Settings → About and in the editor’s Video tab.

presets.qsv.title: Quick Sync (GPU) presets
body: A preset with an Intel **Quick Sync** encoder converts on the server's Intel GPU instead of the CPU. On a 10th-gen Intel i3 it was about **twice as fast** as x264 at the same bitrate, with files of the same size and nearly the same quality. Quick Sync works on Intel iGPUs from 6th generation on, when the server passes the GPU (`/dev/dri`) to EncForge. If `qsv_h264` is listed in Settings → About, it's ready.
### Making one in HandBrake for Windows
1. Open any video, then select the preset to start from.
1. On the **Video** tab, set **Video Encoder** to `H.264 (Intel QSV)` and **Encoder Preset** to `Balanced`. Keep the same average bitrate, or add about 10–15% to match x264's quality.
1. Leave the encoder's **Advanced options** empty: options meant for newer Intel GPUs may not work on the server.
1. **Save New Preset** with its own name, **Export** it, and upload it in [Presets](#presets).

The Intel QSV encoders only appear in HandBrake when your own computer has an Intel GPU. Without one, export the x264 preset instead and edit the `.json` file: set `VideoEncoder` to `qsv_h264` and `VideoPreset` to `balanced`.
### Things to check

- **Quick Sync decoding must stay off.** If the exported file has `"VideoHWDecode": 2`, delete that line: decoding on the GPU fails on 6th–10th gen Intel. The source is decoded on the CPU, which is why it is about twice as fast and not more.
- `H.264 (Intel QSV)` with **Balanced** gave the best results in tests. **Quality** gave the same result, and `H.265 (Intel QSV)` was slower and slightly worse at the same bitrate.
- If the server rejects the preset when you upload it, the message says why, e.g. an encoder it doesn't have.
- To check that a job used the GPU, look for `encoder: H.264 (Intel QSV)` in its [HandBrake log](#job.log). The speed is also higher, e.g. about 60 instead of 30 frames per second.

settings.folders.title: Sources and target folders
body: Folders on the server (not on your computer). NAS shares mounted on the server work too.

- **Sources folders**: where the files to convert are. Add as many as you need with **Add a sources folder**; the Sources panel shows one at a time and can't go above it. Removing a folder from the list deletes nothing.

- **Name** (optional) on a sources folder: a friendly name such as “Downloads”, shown instead of the path in the Sources panel, the folder lists and the Quality view. Each name can be used once, up to 40 characters; an empty name shows the folder’s own name.

- **Protect** on a sources folder: stops its files and folders being deleted or renamed from the app, for example the folder a download client is still seeding from. In the Sources panel such a folder shows **Protected** instead of the Delete button, and the server refuses deletes and renames there too.
- **Target folder**: where converted files are written. The Rename and Merge views work only here.

All must exist. The target cannot be inside a sources folder, and a sources folder cannot be inside another one. In Docker they must be inside the folder mounted into the container (`MEDIA_DIR`, usually `/mnt`).
The output layouts **Source folder name**, **Show and season folders** and **Full source path** are worked out from the sources folder each file is in.

settings.layout.title: Output folder layout
body: Where under the target folder each converted file goes:
- **Source folder name**: `target/Show.S01/episode.mkv`, using only the name of the folder the source is in. Good for season folders.

- **Show and season folders** (TV shows): `target/Show/S01/episode.mkv`. The show and the season come from the folder the source is in: `Show.S01.1080p`, `Show - Season 1` or an episode's own folder such as `Show.S01E05.1080p`; a bare `Season 1` or `S01` folder takes the show name from the folder above it. In a folder with several seasons (`Show.S01-S03`) the season comes from each file's name (`S02E01`). Videos that are not in a season folder go to `target/<source folder>/video.mkv`, as with **Source folder name**.
- **Full source path**: `target/Completed/Show.S01/episode.mkv`, the whole path below the sources folder.
- **All in the target folder**: `target/episode.mkv`.
If the file already exists, the new one gets a suffix (`episode (1).mkv`). The layout applies to files added after the change; queued jobs keep their output path.

settings.language.title: Language
body: The app, its help included, can be shown in English, Italian (Italiano), German (Deutsch), French (Français) or Spanish (Español). Each language is listed in its own name, so it is easy to find whatever language the app is in now.

- **Automatic**: each browser shows the app in its own language (the first one in the browser's language preferences that the app has), English otherwise. Two people can use the app in two languages at the same time.
- **A language**: every browser shows the app in that language.
The choice is saved on the server, like the other settings, and applies as soon as you press **Save changes**. The browser remembers the last language, so the app opens in it straight away next time.

File and folder names, preset names, and error messages from the server, HandBrake or ffmpeg are shown as they are (usually in English). E-mail and push [notifications](#settings.notifications) are always in English.

settings.adding.title: Adding folders
body: - **Include sub-folders**: adding a folder also adds the videos in its sub-folders.
- **Skip files that were already converted**: a file with a converted job is not added again. Use **Convert again** on its job to redo one.
- **Video file extensions**: which files count as videos, separated by commas.
- **Skip files and folders containing these words**: whole words, any case, e.g. `sample` skips `show-sample.mkv` and a `Sample` folder but not `samples.mkv`.

settings.encoding.title: Encoding settings
body: - **CPU priority**: how politely conversions share the CPU with other services on the server (Linux `nice`, 0–19). Higher is gentler and slower only when the server is busy. Ignored when the server runs on Windows without Docker.

- **Check after conversion**: **Full** (every check, with a complete decode), **Quick** (lengths, tracks and readability without decoding) or **Off**. See [Checking converted files](#verify.overview).

settings.subtitles.title: Subtitle settings
body: - **Embedding**: **Only missing languages** (default) embeds a subtitle file when the converted video won't have a subtitle track in that language. Which tracks the video keeps comes from the preset's **Subtitles** tab. **Always** embeds every file; **Never** none.
- A file with no known language is embedded only when the converted video has no subtitles at all.
- **Copying**: **Always** (default) writes every file next to the converted video; **Only those not embedded** skips the embedded ones; **Never** writes none.
- Copies are UTF-8 and named after the converted video, as Plex, Jellyfin and Emby expect: `Movie.en.srt`, `Movie.it.forced.srt`. They follow the video when it is [renamed](#rename.overview).
- **Subtitle file extensions**: which files are looked for. Leave the list empty to ignore subtitle files.
- **Character set of older files**: used to read files that are not UTF-8, often older `.srt` files. If accents look wrong in one file, choose its character set in the [editor](#subtitles.editor).
- MP4 can hold text subtitles only (pictures are copied instead); WebM can't hold any, so they are only copied.

settings.renaming.title: Renaming settings
body: - **Rename files automatically after conversion**: off by default. See [Automatic renaming](#rename.auto).
- **Rule set for automatic renaming**: which [rule set](#rename.rules) is used.
- **Separator**: when the new name is taken, a number is added after it: with `_` you get `name_1.mkv`, `name_2.mkv`.

rename.overview.title: Renaming files
body: Downloaded files have names like `The.Rookie.6x01.Title.ITA.ENG.1080p.NFRip.AAC.x265-Pir8`. The Rename view turns them into `The Rookie S06e01 - Title`, using [rule sets](#rename.rules).
1. On the left, browse the target folder or a sources folder and drag files or folders to the rename list (or use **Rename** on a converted job).
1. Pick the **Rules**. The built-in **Auto** recognises both TV episodes and movies.
1. Look at the [preview](#rename.preview): fix any name by hand, and type a [show name](#rename.showName) where none was found.
1. Press **Rename**. Every batch can be undone from [History](#rename.history).

Files in a sources folder marked **Protect** in [Settings](#settings.folders) can’t be renamed (a download client may still be seeding them), nor can files that are queued or converting. A renamed source still counts as converted, and a watch folder doesn’t take it for a new file.

rename.preview.title: Rename preview
body: Each row shows the current name (small, grey) and the new name. Nothing changes on disk until you press **Rename**.
- **Edit** any new name by typing in it (Enter to confirm, Escape to cancel). An edited row is blue; **undo edit** goes back to the rules' name.
- **Ticks** choose which rows are renamed. Rows with a warning start unticked: check them and tick them when they look right.
- **Warnings** explain what the rules couldn't find, e.g. no episode number, no year, or no show name.
- **TV · S06e01** or **Movie · 2024** shows what was recognised; **no change** means the name is already right.
- If two files would get the same name, or the name is taken by another file in the folder, a number is added: `name_1.mkv` (see [Renaming settings](#settings.renaming)).
- Subtitle files named after a video (`Old.en.srt`) are renamed with it (`New.en.srt`): the row says **and 2 subtitle files**. **Undo** in the history restores them too.
Files in different folders are grouped under their folder.

rename.showName.title: Show name
body: Some files don't have the show name before the episode number, e.g. `S04E07 Reacher Tutti Con Sampson (2026)…`. Type the show name (`Reacher`) and the rows get `Reacher S04e07 - Tutti Con Sampson`; the name is also taken out of the episode title.
- **only where missing** (default): only rows where no show name was found get it. Other shows in the same list keep theirs.
- **for all rows**: every TV row gets this show name, e.g. to shorten a long one or to add a year for a remake: `Silo (2023)`.

rename.rules.title: Rename rule sets
body: A rule set is a list of [steps](#rename.steps) applied in order to each file name (without its extension).
- **Built-in** rule sets (**Auto**, **TV series**, **Movies**) can't be changed: use **Duplicate** to make an editable copy.
- **New** starts a rule set with the [Recognise episode / movie](#rename.smart) step.

- **Import** reads Advanced Renamer presets (`.aren`) as well as rule sets exported from here. Every Advanced Renamer method used for names (replace, remove pattern, remove, add, move, trim, case) becomes a step.
- **Export** (download icon) saves the rule set as a `.json` file, e.g. to copy it to another server.
- Changes are kept only after **Save**; [Try it](#rename.tryIt) shows the result before saving.

rename.steps.title: Rename steps
body: Steps run top to bottom; untick one to switch it off without deleting it. Click a step to edit it.
- **Recognise episode / movie**: builds the whole name from a template. See [Recognise episode / movie](#rename.smart).
- **Remove release tags**: cuts the name at the first tag such as `1080p`, `WEB-DL`, `x265` or `ITA`.
- **Replace**: finds text and replaces it: all, first or last occurrence, matching case or not. With **Regular expression**, `$1`, `$2`… insert the groups found.
- **Remove pattern**: deletes what matches, e.g. `(720p).*$` deletes from `720p` to the end.
- **Remove everything after text**: e.g. after `)`.
- **Remove characters / Add text / Move characters**: work on positions, like Advanced Renamer. Positions change with each file name, so pattern steps are usually safer.
- **Trim characters**: removes the listed characters from both ends.
- **Change case**: Title Case, UPPER, lower or Sentence case.
- **Fix apostrophes**: `L Uomo` → `L'Uomo`, `Dell Oca` → `Dell'Oca`, `Wouldn T` → `Wouldn't`.
- **Collapse spaces**: several spaces become one.
Characters that file names can't contain (`/ \ : * ? " < > |`) are removed or replaced at the end; `:` becomes ` -`.

rename.smart.title: Recognise episode / movie
body: Reads the parts of a release name and builds a clean one.
- **TV**: finds `S01E02`, `S01E01E02` or `1x02`. The show is the text before it, the episode title the text after it, up to the first release tag.
- **Movie**: finds the year (`2024` or `(2024)`); the title is the text before it.
- **Type**: **Auto** treats a name with an episode number as TV and anything else as a movie.
### Templates

`{show}`, `{season}`, `{episode}`, `{title}` and `{year}` are replaced by what was found; season and episode get two digits. A part in `[ ]` disappears when a field inside it is empty: `{show} S{season}e{episode}[ - {title}]` gives `Lanterns S01e01` when there is no episode title.
### Options
- **Title Case words**: capitalises each word, keeping capitals already there (`McLaren`, `INXS`).
- **Fix apostrophes**: `L Osservatore` → `L'Osservatore`.
- **Keep the year in the show name**: `East of Eden 2026 S01E01` becomes `East Of Eden (2026) S01e01`. Off by default; useful for remakes.
- **Extra release tags**: more words that mark the start of the release information.

rename.tryIt.title: Try it
body: Shows what the rule set being edited does to some names, before saving. It starts with the names in your rename list (or a few examples); type or paste any names, one per line.
The **Show name** box works like the one in the [Rename view](#rename.showName).

rename.history.title: Rename history
body: Every batch of renames, newest first, including automatic ones. Click a batch to see each old and new name.
**Undo** gives the files their old names back. A file is skipped if it was deleted or moved since, or if its old name is in use again.

rename.auto.title: Automatic renaming
body: When **Rename files automatically after conversion** is on (Settings → Renaming), each converted file is renamed with the chosen rule set right after its [check](#verify.overview).

To stay safe, a file is renamed only when the rules recognise it **without warnings**. Otherwise the job shows **Needs rename** and you finish it in the [Rename view](#rename.overview). Files that fail the check are not renamed.
Automatic renames appear in [History](#rename.history) and can be undone.

merge.overview.title: Merging files
body: Joins converted files into one MKV, one after the other, for example a film or a concert split into discs or parts. The chapters of every part are kept.
1. On the left, browse the **target folder** and drag the parts (or the folder holding them) to the merge list. Under **Converted** in the queue, **Merge these** does the same.
1. Put the parts [in order](#merge.parts).
1. Read the [compatibility check](#merge.compat): parts that cannot be joined are explained there.
1. Choose the [name and chapters](#merge.options) of the merged file and press **Merge**.

Merging copies the video, audio and subtitles as they are, without converting again, so it takes about as long as copying the files. The merged file is then [checked](#verify.overview) like a conversion: its length must be the parts added together, with the same audio and subtitle tracks as part 1.
Merges run one at a time, alongside conversions. Progress and results are under [Recent merges](#merge.history). The parts are kept unless you choose to delete them.

merge.parts.title: Parts and their order
body: The merged file plays the parts top to bottom. A dropped folder adds its video files in name order (`Disc 1`, `Disc 2`, … `Disc 10`).
- **Drag** a part by its handle, or use the arrows, to change the order.

- **Sort by** puts the parts in name, date, file type or size order, and keeps parts you add later in that order. Dragging or the arrows switch it to **Your order**. The choice is remembered in this browser.
- ✕ takes a part out of the list (the file is not touched).
Each row shows the part’s length, chapters, audio languages, subtitle tracks, picture size and file size, read from the file.

merge.compat.title: Can the parts be joined?
body: Joining files only works when every part has the **same tracks in the same order**. The easiest way is to convert all parts with the same preset.
### Problems that stop the merge (red)
- A different number of video, audio or subtitle tracks, e.g. one part with Italian and English audio and another with Italian only.
- A track in a different format (e.g. AAC in one part, AC-3 in another), or audio with different channels or sample rate.
### Warnings (amber): the merge can go ahead
- A different picture size, or video encoded with slightly different settings (e.g. a different crop). Most players handle it; some may glitch for a moment where the parts join, so check the joins.
- A track in another language: the merged track keeps part 1’s language.

merge.chapters.title: Chapters of the merged file
body: - **Keep each part’s chapters** (default): every chapter keeps its place, moved to where its part starts in the merged file. HandBrake’s generic names (`Chapter 1`, `Chapter 2`…) are renumbered across the whole file; chapters with their own names keep them. A part without chapters gets one chapter named after the file.
- **One chapter per part**: one chapter at the start of each part, named after its file (dots and underscores become spaces).
Open **chapters in the merged file** under the options to see the list before merging.

merge.options.title: Name and options of the merged file
body: - **Name**: suggested from what the parts’ names have in common (`Live Aid - Disc 1`, `Live Aid - Disc 2` → `Live Aid`). The file is always `.mkv`.
- The merged file goes in the **folder of part 1**. If the name is taken, a number is added (`Live Aid_1.mkv`, see [Renaming settings](#settings.renaming)). Nothing is overwritten.
- **Chapters**: see [Chapters of the merged file](#merge.chapters).

- **Delete the parts after a successful merge**: off by default. The parts are deleted only if the merge worked and the [check](#verify.overview) did not fail; if checking is off, they are deleted after the merge. This cannot be undone.
While merging, the file is written as `name.mkv.part` and renamed at the end, so media servers never see a half-written file.

merge.history.title: Recent merges
body: Each merge with its status: **Waiting**, **Reading parts**, **Merging** (with progress), **Checking**, **Merged**, **Failed** or **Cancelled**. A merged file also shows its [check result](#verify.results).
Click a merge to see the output, the parts, any warnings from mkvmerge and the check details.
- ■ cancels a waiting or running merge; the half-written file is deleted and the parts are kept.
- 🗑 removes a finished merge from the list. Files are not touched.

upload.overview.title: Uploading videos
body: Sends video files from your computer into a sources folder on the server, so they can be converted like any other file.
1. In **Convert**, open the folder you want in [Sources](#convert.sources) (choose the sources folder first if you have several).
1. Press **Upload**, or drop files from your computer onto the Sources panel.
1. Optionally press **New folder** to create a sub-folder and upload into it.
1. Press **Upload**. The files go one at a time; a panel in the corner shows the progress and you can keep working.

Only video files are accepted (the extensions in [Adding folders](#settings.adding)), and [subtitle files](#subtitles.overview) to go with them. An existing file is never replaced: you choose to skip it or upload a copy named “name (1)”. The upload stops before it starts if the server lacks the space.
### Interruptions

Keep the browser tab open until the uploads finish. A dropped connection is retried by itself. If the tab was closed, upload the same file to the same folder again: it continues where it stopped. Unfinished uploads are hidden files, removed by themselves after a week; **Cancel** removes one straight away.

quality.overview.title: Quality check
body: Finds video files with an old format, a low resolution or a low bitrate, so you know which ones to replace or convert.
1. In **Quality**, choose folders or files in the **Folders** panel: every sources folder and the target folder are there.
1. Press **Check quality**. Every video inside, sub-folders included, is read with ffprobe (only the file headers, so it is quick; it runs at the CPU priority from [Encoding](#settings.encoding)).
1. The results list the files that **Need attention**. Click the chips to see one kind of problem, or **All**.
What counts as a problem is set in [Settings → Quality check](#settings.quality). Changing a criterion updates the results straight away, without checking again.
- **Add to queue** converts the selected files with the chosen preset (only files in a sources folder).
- **Export CSV** downloads the selected files (or all those listed) as a spreadsheet.

- **Re-check** reads the selected files again, after you fixed or replaced them, and updates their results. A file converted to another format in the same folder (film.avi now film.mkv) takes the old one's place; other files that no longer exist leave the list. New files are only found by a new check.
The last 20 results are kept; pick one in **Result**. A check can run while files are converting.

quality.folders.title: Choosing what to check
body: The Folders panel shows every sources folder and the target folder; choose one in the list at the top.

Tick folders and files (Ctrl-click and Shift-click select several) and press **Check quality**. A folder includes everything inside it. Files matching the words in [Adding folders](#settings.adding) (like “sample”) are skipped.

quality.issues.title: Quality problems
body: - **Old container / video codec / audio codec**: formats in the lists in [Settings](#settings.quality), such as `.avi`, MPEG-4 Part 2 (DivX, Xvid), MPEG-2, WMV or RealVideo.
- **Low resolution**: below the lowest acceptable resolution. Widescreen films with black bars cropped (e.g. 1920×800) count by their width, as 1080p.

- **Low bitrate**: the video bitrate is below the minimum for its resolution. HEVC, AV1 and VP9 need less, so their minimum is lower. **~** means the bitrate was estimated from the file size because the file doesn't state it.
- **Interlaced**: only when turned on in Settings.
- **Unreadable**: ffprobe could not read the file, or it has no video.

naming.overview.title: Naming check
body: Finds the videos in your folders whose name is not the one your rename rules would give them, so a whole library can be tidied up without opening every folder.
1. In **Naming**, pick the **Rules** to check against: **Auto**, **TV series**, **Movies** or one of your own [rule sets](#rename.rules).
1. Choose folders or files in the **Folders** panel and press **Check names**.
1. The [results](#naming.results) list only the files that need a look. Tick the ones to fix and press **Fix in Rename**.
Rename opens with those files and the same rules: check the [preview](#rename.preview), fix names by hand if needed, and press **Rename**. Then press **Check again** here to see what is left.

Only names are read, never the files themselves, so even a whole library takes seconds. Choosing other rules checks the same folders again. Every check is saved: the last 20 are kept, pick one in **Result**. While it runs a bar shows how far it is: first the folders are read, then the names are compared. **Stop** keeps the files checked so far.

naming.folders.title: Choosing what to check
body: The Folders panel shows every sources folder and the target folder, the same ones Rename works on; choose one in the list at the top.
Tick folders and files (Ctrl-click and Shift-click select several) and press **Check names**. A folder includes everything inside it, sub-folders too.

naming.results.title: Naming check results
body: Each file shows its current name and, below it, the name the rules would give it. Files are grouped by folder.
- **Wrong name**: the rules would rename the file.

- **Not recognised**: the rules found something missing, such as no episode number with **TV series** or no year with **Movies**. The file may still have the right name; check it in Rename and type the name by hand if needed.
- **Renamed or moved**: files that are no longer there under that name, for example because you fixed them in Rename. They stay in the result but can’t be selected.

Files that already have the right name are counted but not listed. Files in a protected folder, or queued for conversion, are listed but can’t be selected. **Fix in Rename** takes up to 5000 files at once.

settings.quality.title: Quality check criteria
body: What the [Quality check](#quality.overview) flags. Lists are separated by commas.
- **Lowest acceptable resolution**: files below it are flagged. The resolution counts the width too, so cropped widescreen films keep their class.
- **Lowest acceptable video bitrate**: one value per resolution class (SD, 720p, 1080p, 4K) for H.264, MPEG-4 and similar codecs; 0 turns the check off for that class.
- **Efficient codecs** (HEVC, AV1, VP9 by default) need only the given percentage of those bitrates. With the defaults, a 1080p HEVC file needs 1500 kbps instead of 2500.

- **Old video codecs**, **old audio codecs** and **old containers**: names as ffprobe reports them (`mpeg4`, `msmpeg4v3`, `wmav2`…) and file extensions (`avi`, `wmv`…). Empty a list to turn that check off.
- **Flag interlaced video**: off by default, because many TV recordings are interlaced on purpose.

download.overview.title: Downloading files
body: Copies files from the server to your computer: from any sources folder or the target folder, in every panel that lists folders (Sources, Rename, Merge, Quality and Naming).
- Point at a file or folder and press its download arrow, or tick several and press **Download**.
- **One file** downloads straight away. The browser's own download list shows the progress, and an interrupted download can be resumed there.

- **A folder** (sub-folders included) comes as **one ZIP file** that keeps the folders inside. The files are stored as they are, not compressed, so it starts at once and the browser knows the size. A ZIP download that is interrupted must start again.
- **Several files** can come as one ZIP or as separate files. For separate files, your browser may ask once whether the site may download several files.
A converted file can also be downloaded from its job details (**download converted file**). Hidden files and unfinished conversions (`.part`) are left out of ZIP files.

A video with [subtitle files](#subtitles.overview) next to it (e.g. `Movie.en.srt`, or a `Subs` folder in the sources) asks whether to download them too, as one ZIP; when several files are downloaded, the videos' subtitle files are included. In the job details, **Download with subtitles (ZIP)** does the same for a converted video.

delete.overview.title: Deleting source files
body: Removes files or folders from a sources folder on the server, for example a download you have finished converting.
1. In **Convert**, tick the files or folders in [Sources](#convert.sources).
1. Press **Delete** (or the Delete key).
1. The confirmation shows exactly what will go: how many files, how much space, and everything inside a chosen folder. Press **Delete** to confirm; **Cancel** is the default.
A video's [subtitle files](#subtitles.overview) (e.g. `Movie.en.srt`, or the ones in its `Subs` folder) are deleted with it; the confirmation lists them.
Deleting cannot be undone. If a download client such as Deluge is still seeding the files, it will report them as missing.
### What is refused
- Files that are queued, converting or paused, and folders that contain one. Remove them from the queue first.
- Anything in a sources folder marked **Protect** in [Settings](#settings.folders).
- A sources folder itself (remove it from the list in [Settings](#settings.folders) instead; that deletes nothing).
- Anything in the target folder: converted files are not deleted from here.

backup.overview.title: Backup and restore
body: A backup holds the app's own data: settings (folders, quality criteria…), presets, rename rule sets, the job list and history, rename history, merges, quality check and naming check results. Optionally it also holds the HandBrake log of each job. Video files are never part of it.
It is in [Settings](#settings.folders) → **Backup and restore**.
- **Download backup** saves a ZIP file on your computer.
- **Save on the server** keeps one in the app's data folder (`data/backups`). The newest 10 are kept.
### Restoring
1. **Choose a backup file…** from your computer, or pick one under **Backups on the server**.
1. Check what it holds: the table compares the backup with the current data, and folders that don't exist on this server are pointed out.
1. Choose **Configuration only** (settings, presets and rename rules; jobs and history stay) or **Everything** (also jobs and their logs, histories, merges, quality and naming results).
1. Press **Restore…** and confirm. The page reloads afterwards.
Before every restore the current data is saved on the server as **Before a restore**, so a restore can be undone by restoring that one.
A restore never starts the queue. **Everything** can't be restored while a conversion, merge, quality check or upload is running.
The e-mail password for [notifications](#settings.notifications) is part of the settings, so it is in every backup: keep backup files somewhere private.

queue.eta.title: How long the queue still needs
body: Above the jobs the Queue shows how much conversion time is left and when it will be done; each queued job shows its own estimate, and the top bar the total.

The estimate is each source’s length × how fast this server converted similar files before: the median of the last 20 conversions with the **same preset** (encode plus the [check after conversion](#verify.overview)). For a preset with no history, all presets together are used; with no history at all, the speed of the job converting now.
- A job whose source hasn’t been read yet gets the average length of the others (“some lengths guessed”).
- With a [conversion window](#settings.schedule), the finish time follows it: jobs only start inside the window, and one that is converting when it closes is finished first.
- Other work on the server (media server transcoding, a quality check) slows conversions down, so treat the time as a guide.

settings.schedule.title: Conversion window
body: Converts only at certain times, e.g. overnight, so encoding doesn’t slow down a media server or other services during the day.
- **Opens at / Closes at**: when the closing time is earlier than the opening time (23:00 → 07:00) the window runs overnight. The same time for both means all day.
- **Days** are the days the window **opens**: Friday with 23:00 → 07:00 ends on Saturday morning.
- Outside the window the queue doesn’t start a new job. A job that is converting when the window closes is finished first.

- **Start the queue by itself when the window opens**: if jobs are waiting and the queue is stopped, it starts when the window opens. Pressing Stop during the window is respected until the next opening.
The top bar shows the window’s state (open until …, or when it opens next); click it to come here.
The window follows the **server’s clock**. If the server’s time zone differs from yours, this page says so: set `TZ` in the server’s `.env` (e.g. `TZ=Europe/London`) and restart the container.

settings.watch.title: Watch folders
body: New videos that appear in a watch folder are added to the queue by themselves, with the preset chosen for that folder (or the default one).

Two ways to add one: **Watch** next to the folder path in the Sources panel (Convert) watches the open folder with the default preset, or **Add a watch folder…** here, which opens a folder browser (**Browse…** changes the folder of an existing row). In the Sources panel watched folders show an eye, and the open folder shows **Watched**; click it to come here.
- A watch folder must be inside one of the [sources folders](#settings.folders). Watch folders can’t be inside each other.
- Files already in a folder when you add it are **left alone**; drag them into the queue yourself if you want them. Each file is added **once**, even if you later remove its job.

- A file is added only after it has **stopped changing** for the quiet time you set (10 minutes by default), so downloads and copies in progress are not picked up. The folders are looked at every few minutes, because file system events don’t arrive over NFS or SMB.
- For a download client, watch the folder **completed** downloads are moved to, not the one it downloads into: a paused download could otherwise look finished.
- The usual rules for adding apply: exclude words such as `sample`, video extensions, and “Skip files that were already converted”.
- **Start the queue after adding files**: otherwise they wait for **Start**. With a [conversion window](#settings.schedule), the queue then waits for the window.
**Activity** shows files waiting to settle, the last files added or skipped, and problems such as a missing folder. **Look now** checks straight away.

settings.notifications.title: Notifications
body: The server can tell you when the queue finishes, a conversion or its check fails, each file is converted, a watch folder adds files, or a scheduled backup fails. Choose the events at the top; e-mail and the webhooks follow that list, unless a webhook has its own.
### Webhooks

A JSON `POST` per message to a URL: an n8n **Webhook** node, a Home Assistant webhook trigger, ntfy, Gotify… Add as many as you need (up to 10) with **Add a webhook**; each has a name, an on/off switch, its URL and optional extra headers, e.g. `Authorization: Bearer …`, one per line.
- Each webhook gets **the events chosen above**, or **only these events**: for example everything to n8n, but only “the queue finished” to Home Assistant.
- The body has `event`, `title`, `message` (plain text), `url` (the app address, if set), `at` and `data` (the job or the run’s details).
### E-mail
Sent through your SMTP server. Typical settings: **STARTTLS** on port 587, **TLS** on 465. For Gmail and Outlook, use an **app password**, not your normal one.
- The password is stored on the server and never sent back to the browser; leave the box empty to keep it.
- It is part of the settings, so it is in [backups](#backup.overview).
**Send a test** uses what is on the screen, before you save. **Recently sent** lists the last messages and any error.
### This browser

The tab title always shows the progress (“42% · Show S01e02.mkv”, “✓ Queue finished”). Desktop notifications can appear while the tab is in the background; browsers allow them only on `https://` pages or `localhost`, so on a plain `http://` address use e-mail or a webhook instead.

stats.overview.title: Stats
body: What the server has converted over the chosen period: files, space saved, length of video converted and the work it took, and the speed (× real time: 2× means an hour of video took 30 minutes, check included).
- **Files converted per day** (or per month for long periods): hover a column for its details, or switch to **Table**.
- **Check after conversion**: how many converted files passed, had warnings or failed the [check](#verify.overview).
- **By preset**: compare presets on speed and size reduction.
Every conversion that started is recorded when it finishes. **Clear finished** in the Queue doesn’t remove it from these figures. The same history gives the [queue finish time](#queue.eta).

backup.schedule.title: Scheduled backups
body: Makes a [backup](#backup.overview) by itself every day or every week at the time you choose, and keeps the newest ones (14 by default). Older scheduled backups are deleted; other files in the folder are never touched.

- **Folder on the server**: empty means the app’s own `data/backups`. To keep backups off the server, use a network share that is mounted on it, e.g. a folder on the NAS. With Docker the folder must be inside the folder mounted into the container (`MEDIA_DIR`, usually `/mnt`). **Browse…** picks a folder under the sources or target folders; any other path can be typed.
- The folder must exist and be writable when you turn the schedule on.

- If the server was off or the share was not mounted at backup time, the backup is made as soon as possible. A failed backup is tried again after 30 minutes, and can send a [notification](#settings.notifications) (“A scheduled backup failed”).
- Each file is written under a temporary name and renamed when complete, so a half-written backup never appears in the folder.
- **Back up now** makes one straight away with the saved settings.
Scheduled backups are listed under **Kept by the schedule**, where they can be restored, downloaded or deleted like the others.
The backup holds the settings, so also the e-mail password for notifications: keep the folder private.

presets.editor.title: Editing a preset
body: The editor works like the HandBrake desktop app. The name, category and description are at the top; the settings are in tabs:
- **Summary**: the container (MP4, MKV, WebM, MOV), web optimisation, chapter markers and metadata.
- **Dimensions**: rotation and flipping, cropping (automatic removes black bars), the **resolution limit** (bigger sources are scaled down to it), anamorphic and borders.

- **Filters**: detelecine, interlace detection and deinterlacing, deblock, denoise, chroma smooth, sharpen, colourspace and greyscale. A filter set to **Custom** takes HandBrake’s own `key=value:key=value` settings.
- **Video**: the encoder, frame rate, quality (constant quality or average bitrate) and the encoder’s preset, tune, profile, level and advanced options.
- **Audio**: which source tracks are kept (by language), the encoders each track gets, auto passthru and track names.
- **Subtitles**: which subtitle tracks are kept, foreign audio scan, closed captions and burn-in.
- **JSON**: every setting as HandBrake stores it, for the few the tabs don’t show. **Apply to the form** takes your JSON edits.

The encoders and their preset, tune, profile and level lists come from this server’s HandBrakeCLI, so the editor offers only what it can run. Encoders that can’t go into the chosen container are greyed out.
### Saving
- **Save** replaces the preset. **Save as new…** keeps it as it was and saves your changes as a new preset.
- When you open a preset, the server lets HandBrakeCLI read it, so presets from older HandBrake versions are upgraded and every setting is filled in. Saving checks the preset with HandBrakeCLI again.
- Problems are listed above the tabs. A red one (e.g. an H.265 encoder with a WebM container) must be fixed before saving; a yellow one is a warning, e.g. an encoder this server doesn’t have.
- Jobs already in the queue keep the settings they were added with. Watch folders use the new settings for files they add from now on.
- Leaving with unsaved changes asks first.

presets.new.title: New preset
body: **New** (Presets page) makes a preset and opens it in the [editor](#presets.editor).
- **A HandBrake preset**: one of the presets built into HandBrake, such as “Fast 1080p30”, “H.265 MKV 1080p30” or the device presets. The list comes from this server’s HandBrakeCLI.
- **One of your presets**: a copy, like **Duplicate**.
Give it a name (and optionally a category, which groups presets in the list, and a description). Two presets can share a name only in different categories.
The new preset is saved straight away: change it in the editor, or delete it if you change your mind.

settings.security.title: Security: login
body: EncForge has no login until you turn it on. While it is off, anyone who can open the page can browse, convert, rename and **delete files**, and change the settings.
To turn it on:
1. Set a password (at least 8 characters).
2. Turn on **Login**. This browser stays signed in; every other browser shows a sign-in page.
- A browser stays signed in until it has not been used for 30 days. **Sign out** (top right) ends it at once.
- **Changing the password** signs every other browser out, and so does **Sign out other browsers**.
- After 5 wrong passwords from one address, signing in from there is blocked for 15 minutes.
- Other programs use [API keys](#settings.apiKeys) instead of the password.

**Forgot the password?** Start the app with the environment variable `DISABLE_LOGIN=true` (with Docker: add it to `.env` and recreate the container). Login is then off, and a new password can be set without the current one. Remove the variable and restart to turn login back on.
The password, the signed-in browsers and the API keys are not in [backups](#backup.overview), and a restore never changes them.
Login protects the app, not the connection: for access from outside your network, use a VPN or a reverse proxy with HTTPS.

settings.apiKeys.title: API keys
body: API keys let other programs (scripts, n8n, Home Assistant…) use EncForge’s API: the same requests the web app makes, under `/api/`.
The program sends the key with every request, in either header:
- `Authorization: Bearer ef_…`
- `X-API-Key: ef_…`
Each key has an access level:
- **Read only**: the queue, jobs, presets, settings (without webhook headers, which often hold tokens) and statistics; listing folders and downloading files.
- **Queue**: also adding and controlling jobs, starting and stopping the queue, uploading files, making folders, quality and naming checks.
- **Full**: everything else too: settings, presets and rename rule sets, renaming and deleting files, merging, backups and restore.
No key can manage login or API keys: that is done here, in a signed-in browser.
- The key is shown once, when it is created. Only a fingerprint of it is kept, so a lost key cannot be shown again: revoke it and create a new one.
- The list shows when each key was last used, and from which address.
- While [login](#settings.security) is off, keys are optional; but a key that is sent is checked, so an integration can be tested before turning login on.
Example: add a file to the queue with the default preset (add `"presetId"` to choose another):
`curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ef_…" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"paths":["/mnt/downloads/Movie.mkv"]}' http://server:8095/api/jobs`
